This matches prepare_unit(), which forces those flags on canonical_parts, and validate_pure_parts()/check_target(), which reject the library root as a target. It is therefore metadata required by canonical-home validation, not a whole-prayer provider. Acceptable as explained.

CODE — approved. The validate_occurrence_controls change requires language and text, allows only the extra key `type`, and restricts `type` (defaulting to 'instruction') to {'instruction','description'}. It correctly rejects other strings, non-strings (True, None) and unexpected keys such as 'target'. Short-circuit order is safe: isinstance(dict) is checked before set(i). The same validator guards the canonical_text and prepare_documents paths, so the restriction also applies to instructions in a canonical home. The edition/settings text edits only remove 'in progress' wording. Draft output still carries 'DRAFT: independent adjudication pending.', so the metadata stays truthful.

TESTS — adequate. The new test covers description emission into the host, no note leaking into the shared words document, three invalid type values and an unexpected key.
